reviewer.role: separate semantic reviewer (Claude Code agent, Opus 5.5); did not operate the run or author the cases
reviewer.method: Parsed run/journal.jsonl with python3; rated each reached phase on the last result of that phase; every quote below was checked as an exact substring of the cited journal line. No coding-agent CLI was run and no network request was made.
reviewer.independence_limit: Single AI reviewer from the same model family as the evaluated agent. Blocking-failure, dispute and alternative-solution adjudication by a second contributor is still required.

comparison_contracts: As frozen in the plan: wrapper 32,000 input bytes, native contract 4, D022 weaken-and-report gates, provisional open questions must carry owner-unknown keys; baseline 64,000 input bytes, transcript only, strict JSON checks, no canonical state, provenance or downgrade reporting. The baseline input carries remaining_questions; the wrapper input does not.
rating_rules_applied: Phase result = last delivered output of that phase (base: the result before the variation or job end; variation: the last result after the variation text).

For the two question-limit stops, dimensions were rated on the last delivered interim output and recommendation_fit is not checked because the closing result was not reached; protocol stops are recorded separately from semantic failures.
Bundled questions are not by themselves a clarification failure (both approaches bundled often); the overrun is recorded as the protocol stop.
Wrapper view dimensions are judged from the state that the frozen controller renders and from the /api/export response; no rendered replay exists in the evidence (see limitations).

Minor issues are presentation or wording problems that do not change a decision; they are recorded but do not fail a dimension. Assumptions presented as facts and asserted legal or feature outcomes do fail the relevant dimension.
Undisclosed operator facts were not required; inferable checks were satisfied by questions, open decisions or conditional advice.

summary.strict_reading_alternative: If plan.review.required_evidence ("No rendered check means view dimensions remain not checked") is applied literally, every wrapper owner_view_clarity and brief_and_view_consistency rating becomes not checked and the wrapper passes 0 of 10 phases; baseline ratings are unchanged.

findings: No blocking failure in any delivered result for either approach. Every delivered recommendation chose an existing tool, a manual workflow or no build; no secrets or private documents were requested; no zero-price or safety guarantee was made.

Phases passed: wrapper 8 of 10, baseline 7 of 10. Wrapper misses: C03 (protocol stop) and C07 (asserted legal and provider-feature outcomes). Baseline misses: C01 (protocol stop) and both C05 phases (an inference stated as fact in the Owner View, plus an unknown attributed to the owner for an unasked budget question). The margin is within one-shot noise and depends on judgment calls; it is not evidence of a general wrapper advantage.

One protocol stop each. The C03-wrapper stop is genuine under the rule, but the wrapper never sees the counted-request budget (the baseline input carries remaining_questions), so it cannot avoid an overrun. The C01-baseline stop follows from an operator overcount (OD-2).

Wrapper did better on unknown provenance: every owner_unknowns entry is bound to a question actually asked and carried as a keyed open question, and V02 was kept as a separate keyed unknown with a one-download next step. Its hidden requirements were also more specific (C06 transcripts need the same care and deletion relies on trust; C04 guests listed without asking; C05 GPS-free summary for the physiotherapist).

Baseline did better on cost and burden: 25 calls and 788 s against 33 calls and 1,943 s, about one third of the reported cost, and fewer counted questions (26 against 35). Its C07 legal advice was correctly hedged where the wrapper asserted outcomes.
The wrapper's D022 weakening path was never exercised: 0 downgrades in 33 adoptions, so the "Check these" list stayed empty and the run gives no evidence that the weakening gates protected the owner.

The wrapper's removed/added advice lists are noisy enough to obscure the real change: 300 removed and 379 added items, about half of them rewordings, and up to 76 items per adoption at variations. Comparing by exact text produces this noise; a reword-tolerant comparison or a collapsed default view is needed before the list helps an owner.

Both approaches handled all three variations correctly: the V01 split rule stayed open, the V02 unknown was preserved without assertion, and the V03 keep rule and leave-and-list behaviour went into the criteria with no deletion.
limitations: Single AI reviewer of the same model family; a second contributor must adjudicate blocking-failure absence, the three non-blocking dimension failures, the two protocol stops and OD-1/OD-2 before any acceptance claim.
No rendered replay, browser view or download of the wrapper exists in the evidence; wrapper view ratings are content-derived (see strict_reading_alternative). Owner comprehension is untested.
The operator implemented the wrapper; the cases were authored by an agent. Seven one-shot cases do not support causal or general claims.
Ratings use only disclosed owner evidence; differences in what each approach was told (equal access, unequal questions) limit direct comparison per case.
Quote checks establish that each quoted passage exists at the cited line, not that the judgment is correct.
